Package de.l9g.scm.oauth2.plugin

Class TokenVerifier

java.lang.Object
de.l9g.scm.oauth2.plugin.TokenVerifier
public class TokenVerifier extends Object
Verifies the tokens of the identity provider: signature first, then the claims.

Two levels of strictness

The id token is an authentication statement and is therefore validated strictly according to OIDC Core 3.1.3.7 — a token which is present but invalid aborts the login. The access token is only read to import roles; an anomaly there costs the roles, but does not fail the login, since the token was received over an authenticated tls connection and the identity itself comes from the userinfo endpoint.

What happens without key material

Verification needs either a key set url (from the discovery document or from the configuration) or, for the HS family, the client secret. If neither is available, no token is verified and none is used: the id token is discarded and no roles are imported, each with a warning naming the missing configuration. Data which cannot be verified is never trusted.

    • verifyIdToken

      public Optional<com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.JsonNode> verifyIdToken(String idToken, String expectedNonce)
      Verifies an id token.
      Parameters:
      idToken - id token of the token response, may be null if the provider does not issue one
      expectedNonce - nonce of the authorization request; if it is set, the token has to carry the same value
      Returns:
      the verified claims, empty if there is no token or if it cannot be verified for lack of key material
      Throws:
      org.apache.shiro.authc.AuthenticationException - if a token is present but invalid
